plant.description: A water reservoir. Input u in [0,1] is pump duty and raises the level; the reservoir drains on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a noisy level reading.

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Measures direction, rate of rise, and lag at a moderate input to estimate gain and settling time needed to choose hold-input for target.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain reservoir hypothesis is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.22 toward 0.4-0.6 over 15s with positive slope in last seconds if not yet settled, clearly above noise and well below 0.7 actual.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Estimates high-input gain and steady-state input needed to hold 0.6, which decides whether target is reachable and what feedforward to use.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain low-equilibrium hypothesis is right, y rises from ~0.13 toward 0.25-0.35 over 8s with positive slope in last seconds and stays well below 0.5; a flat or falling trace would challenge positive gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Measures high-input equilibrium and settling by extending the same 0.8 hold to separate linear low-gain settling near 0.27 from nonlinear higher equilibrium, which decides required feedforward for 0.6 and reachability.
experiments.expected_observation: If higher-gain/nonlinear hypothesis is right, y continues rising from ~0.26 toward 0.32-0.40 over 7s with sustained positive slope and stays below 0.45; if linear low-gain hypothesis is right, y flattens near ~0.27 with slope decaying to ~0.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Extends the same 0.8 hold to estimate high-level equilibrium and settling time constant, separating linear ~0.27 cap from nonlinear ~0.5-0.7 equilibrium, which sets the feedforward u needed to hold 0.6.
experiments.expected_observation: If nonlinear higher-gain hypothesis is right, y rises from ~0.43 toward ~0.48-0.52 over 5s with sustained positive slope ~0.015-0.025 and stays below 0.55 actual; flattening near 0.43 would support linear low equilibrium and challenge H8.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Measures self-drain rate and fall time constant at u=0, which sets integral action and predicts how fast level falls from the band and is needed before tuning a controller to hold 0.6.
experiments.expected_observation: If self-drain hypothesis is right, y decays monotonically from ~0.51 toward ~0.2-0.3 over 20s with negative slope in last seconds if not yet settled, noise +/-0.02, staying below 0.55 and well above 0.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Estimates intermediate gain and trajectory toward target at u=0.7 to interpolate feedforward for 0.6 and test reachability.
experiments.expected_observation: If nonlinear increasing-gain hypothesis is right, y rises from ~0.15 toward ~0.28-0.35 over 9s with sustained positive slope ~0.015-0.022 in last seconds and stays below 0.40 actual; flattening near 0.20 would challenge H8 and support linear low-gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Distinguishes cold-start delay from permanent low-y dead-zone and measures intermediate slope at u=0.7 to interpolate feedforward for 0.6, which sets integral time and avoids under-actuation.
experiments.expected_observation: If delay-plus-rising-gain hypothesis is right, y accelerates from ~0.15 toward ~0.22-0.28 over 9s with slope ~0.013 rising to ~0.015-0.020 in last seconds and stays below 0.35; continued flat near 0.15 would indicate dead-zone/low gain at low y.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Measures high-u rise rate at 0.32-0.45 to estimate gain vs u and interpolate feedforward u needed to hold 0.6, which decides reachability and controller bias.
experiments.expected_observation: If increasing-gain positive-gain hypothesis is right, y rises from ~0.32 toward ~0.40-0.45 over 5s with sustained positive slope ~0.015-0.022 in last seconds and stays below 0.50 actual; flattening near 0.32 or fall would challenge H1/H8.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Distinguishes u=0.8 equilibrium ~0.6-0.8 (H9) from linear ~0.27 cap (H5) by measuring rise slope at y~0.42-0.52; this sets feedforward u needed to hold 0.6 and decides reachability, the last blocker for controller design.
experiments.expected_observation: If increasing-gain H8/H9 is right, y rises from ~0.42 toward ~0.50-0.53 over 5s with sustained positive slope ~0.015-0.022 in last seconds and stays below ~0.55 actual; flattening near 0.42 or fall toward 0.27 would support linear cap and challenge H8/H9.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Tests whether u=0.8 equilibrium exceeds 0.6 and measures rise slope inside approach to band to pin feedforward for 0.6, the last blocker for controller design.
experiments.expected_observation: If increasing-gain H8/H9 is right, y rises from ~0.52 toward ~0.58-0.62 over 4s with sustained positive slope ~0.015-0.022 in last seconds and stays below ~0.65 actual; flattening near 0.52 or fall would challenge H1/H8/H9.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Brackets steady-state u needed to hold 0.6 by measuring slope at 0.59 under u=0.6, separating H9 (0.8 holds/overshoots) from H10 (0.7 holds) to set controller feedforward.
experiments.expected_observation: If H8/H9 right (u=0.8 eq 0.65-0.85, u=0.7 eq 0.45-0.65), stepping 0.8->0.6 from ~0.59 yields flat to slowly falling trace staying ~0.53-0.62 with slope ~-0.015 to +0.005 in last seconds and below 0.65; sustained rise would imply lower feedforward and challenge H7/H8.

ledger.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases level y with positive steady-state gain.
At u=0 the level decays over time due to self-drain and does not self-hold.

There is no permanent dead-zone: u=0.4 holds ~0.13 and 0.4->0.8 rises promptly, but cold start 0->0.7 shows ~5-7s lag before rise; E6 flat then E7 sustained rise and E8/E9/E10/E11 immediate response when warm confirms delay not dead-zone.

Response has seconds-scale lag plus slow settling: ~1-2s lag when already pumping vs ~5-7s cold-start delay, time constant ~10-25s; settling takes >20s with slopes still ~0.02/s at u=0.8/0.9 and -0.019/s at u=0 and +0.0109/s 4s after 0.8->0.6 step showing momentum carryover.
Steady-state response is approximately linear and u in 0.3-0.6 holds y near target 0.6.
Sensor noise std is small (~0.02-0.03) so multi-second trends are interpretable.
Steady-state at u=0.4 is ~0.13, but gain is strongly nonlinear so required u to hold 0.6 is ~0.5-0.65, not linear extrapolation; E11 0.8->0.6 from 0.59 rose to 0.633 showing 0.6 holds/rises.

Gain increases with u so u=0.8 equilibrium is substantially above linear extrapolation from u=0.4 (>0.27), leaving target 0.6 reachable; E7 at u=0.7 exceeds linear 0.23 and E8/E9/E10 sustain ~0.016-0.021/s at y~0.38-0.59 and E11 rises at 0.6.
Equilibrium at u=0.8 is ~0.70-0.90 and overshoots 0.6; E10 ended at 0.591 still rising at 0.0161/s after ~24s total at 0.8 and E11 shows even u=0.6 rises at 0.63.
Steady-state at u=0.7 is ~0.55-0.80, likely at/above 0.6; E7 ended at 0.315 still rising at 0.016/s after 18s total and E11 implies 0.6 alone is near/above equilibrium.

Steady-state at u=0.6 is at or above ~0.63; E11 stepped 0.8->0.6 at ~0.59 and rose to 0.633 with +0.0109/s over 4s, though 4s is short vs 10-25s time constant so part may be momentum from prior 0.8 rise.
